run.procedureSummary: Each cycle runs five steps in this order, and each step finishes for all six chambers before the next one starts. (1) Feed: add that cycle's feed figure to each chamber, including PUPAL chambers, with no capacity limit. (2) Overflow: go through chambers 1 to 6 in turn. Any amount over a chamber's capacity is cut back to capacity and the excess added to the next chamber before that chamber is checked, so overflow can cascade. Chamber 6's excess goes to the loss tally. (3) Check: look at each chamber once, using its state at the start of the step. A LARVAL chamber with quantity at or above its upper mark becomes PUPAL. A PUPAL chamber with quantity at or below its lower mark becomes LARVAL. Otherwise the state stays the same. (4) Metabolism: first work out every amount from the quantities after the check, then move them all at once. A LARVAL chamber loses floor(q/4) to the tally. A PUPAL chamber loses floor(q/2), which goes to the previous chamber (chamber 1's goes to the tally). There is no capacity enforcement here, so an overfull chamber stays overfull until the next cycle's overflow. (5) Moult: if the line total after metabolism is strictly greater than 38, each chamber becomes floor(q/2) and the removed amount, q - floor(q/2), goes to the tally.

openPoints.point: Whether the moult trigger 'over 38' is strict
openPoints.assumption: Strictly greater than 38. A total of exactly 38 does not fire it. This matters in cycle 5, where the total after metabolism is exactly 38, so no moult happens.

openPoints.point: What gets tallied in a moult when halving rounds down
openPoints.assumption: The new quantity is floor(q/2) and the removed amount is q - floor(q/2), which is ceil(q/2). All of it goes to the tally.

openPoints.point: When the moult total is measured
openPoints.assumption: After metabolism in the same cycle. The moult is the fifth step, after all earlier steps finish.

openPoints.point: Whether a chamber can change state twice in one check, or whether order matters within the check
openPoints.assumption: Each chamber is checked once against its state and quantity at the start of the step, so there is at most one change per chamber per check. The meaning of 'routinely' is unclear, so I read it as the normal check rule with no special condition.

openPoints.point: Which quantities metabolism amounts are based on
openPoints.assumption: The quantities after the check step, all taken before any mass moves, so mass a PUPAL chamber receives from the next chamber does not change what it loses in the same step.

openPoints.point: What happens when reabsorption pushes a chamber over capacity
openPoints.assumption: Following 'Overfull chambers wait for next overflow', nothing is trimmed until the next cycle's overflow step. The moult also halves overfull chambers. Chamber 2 ends cycle 5 at 10, above its capacity of 8, and that is reported as it stands.
Chambers are processed in order 1 to 6. A chamber's excess is added to the next chamber before that chamber is checked against capacity.

openPoints.point: Whether a PUPAL chamber reabsorbs into a PUPAL or LARVAL neighbour
openPoints.assumption: It reabsorbs into the previous chamber whatever that chamber's state.

run.notes: The arithmetic comes from a Python script, C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\sim.py. I also checked cycle 1 by hand and got the same figures. The script works only inside the desk folder. Two points are sensitive to interpretation. First, in cycle 5 the total is exactly 38, so under the strict 'over 38' reading the moult does not fire; if it did, the end figures would be different. Second, chamber 2 ends at 10, above its capacity of 8, because the mass it reabsorbed waits for the next overflow and there is no further cycle.
